future.mizu: Parallel Future Backend using ‘mizu’

Note: This package is an early prototype under development.

Introduction

The future package provides a generic API for using futures in R. A future is a simple yet powerful mechanism to evaluate an R expression and retrieve its value at some point in time. Futures can be resolved in many different ways depending on which strategy is used. There are various types of synchronous and asynchronous futures to choose from in the future package.

This package, future.mizu, provides a type of futures that utilizes the mizu package.

For example,

library(future)
plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession)

x %<-% { Sys.sleep(5); 3.14 }
y %<-% { Sys.sleep(5); 2.71 }
x + y
#> [1] 5.85

This is obviously a toy example to illustrate what futures look like and how to work with them. For further examples on how to use futures, see the vignettes of the future package as well as those of future.apply, furrr, and doFuture. You can also use futurize to parallelize your existing map-reduce code, e.g. lapply(xs, fcn) |> futurize().

Using the future.mizu backend

The future.mizu package implements a future backend wrapper for mizu.

Backend Description Alternative in future package
mizu_multisession parallel evaluation in separate R processes (on current machine) plan(multisession)

Advantages of mizu futures

The mizu package runs parallel R workers on the local machine, where the main R process and the workers communicate via shared memory (POSIX shared memory on Linux and macOS, and Win32 file mappings on Windows) instead of through sockets. Communication is cheap enough that work can be divided into small pieces, and large vectors and data frames can be read in place, without being copied. The mizu_multisession futures make these properties available to everything that is built on the Future API, e.g. future.apply, furrr, doFuture, and futurize, without having to change any code.

Because of this, mizu_multisession futures behave like any other future: the code does not have to change, the results are identical, and output and conditions, e.g. cat(), message(), and warning(), are relayed to the main R session as usual.

Limitations

  • The workers always run on the local machine. For workers on other machines, or on a high-performance compute (HPC) cluster, use another future backend.

  • At most 64 workers are supported by mizu.

  • Cancelling a future is advisory. A future that is already running on a worker cannot be interrupted; it runs to completion and its result is discarded.

  • Using a single worker, plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession, workers = 1), falls back to sequential processing in the current R process, unless the number of workers is protected by I(), e.g. workers = I(1).

Demos

The future package provides a demo using futures for calculating a set of Mandelbrot planes. The demo does not assume anything about what type of futures are used. The user has full control of how futures are evaluated. For instance, to use mizu_multisession futures, run the demo as:

library(future)
plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession)

demo("mandelbrot", package = "future", ask = FALSE)

Installation

The package is not yet available on CRAN. To install the development version from GitHub, use:

remotes::install_github("futureverse/future.mizu")

This will install the package from source.
